title: Back up and practise recovery
summary: A backup is another copy of important data. A useful backup must be readable and restorable, not merely present.
introduction: A backup is another copy of important data. A useful backup must be readable and restorable, not merely present. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain back up and practise recovery
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.title: Back up and practise recovery

blocks.text: The practice checks whether the saved copy can actually help after loss.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Describe how to test a backup without deleting the original.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: A copy on the same failing disk may be lost with the original.
For more detail later, use this [Cybersecurity Fundamentals further reading](https://www.cisa.gov/secure-our-world).
